claims.text: DNS TTL limits the duration a resolver can reuse a cached resource record before consulting its source again.
A record with a zero TTL is usable for the current transaction but is not retained in the cache for later requests.
For example, a positive lifetime of 3600 seconds permits reuse for up to one hour; a shorter interval makes changes visible sooner.
A resolver needs to track remaining lifetime rather than assume every cached record stays valid indefinitely.
When planning a record change, the operator should consider copies that were cached under the old lifetime.
Reducing the configured lifetime does not retroactively edit those copies, so the change plan must account for existing cache contents and future queries.

Lunar phases occur because an observer on Earth sees different fractions of the sunlit half of the Moon as it moves around our planet.
Ordinary phases are not produced by Earth casting its shadow on the Moon.
The repeating interval from one new moon to the next averages about 29.5 days, longer than the roughly 27.3 days needed to orbit relative to distant stars.
A calendar for observing the Moon should distinguish the phase cycle from the orbital period measured against the stars.
During one orbit, Earth also moves along its path around the Sun, so the Moon must travel farther to restore the same lighting geometry.
An observer can use the changing illuminated fraction to describe the phase without confusing it with a lunar eclipse.

Gregorian leap year rules add a February day in years divisible by four, except century years that are not also divisible by four hundred.
The year 2000 qualified because it was divisible by 400, whereas 1900 did not qualify even though it was divisible by four.
This century exception changes the simpler rule used by the Julian calendar and keeps the civil year closer to the seasonal year.
Calendar software should implement the complete divisibility test rather than only checking whether a year divides by four.
A useful test suite includes an ordinary common year, an ordinary leap year, a century excluded by the exception, and a century included by the four hundred rule.
The examples 1900 and 2000 therefore exercise different branches and help catch a common implementation mistake.

PNG compression is lossless: decoding restores the encoded sample values without discarding image information to obtain a smaller file.
PNG supports an optional alpha channel for partial pixel transparency, with values representing degrees of opacity rather than only a binary visible or invisible choice.
This makes the format useful when crisp graphics and transparency must survive storage and decoding with predictable sample values.
A graphics pipeline should distinguish the compression method from earlier editing steps such as palette reduction or resizing.
Those editing choices can change samples before the file is written, even though the PNG compression itself is lossless.
When exporting a translucent graphic, the author should preserve the alpha channel and check the rendered result against both light and dark backgrounds to inspect edge appearance.
